To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

infection of human epithelia with pathogenic neisseria results in multiple changes in lysosomal function, including reduced levels of LAMP1, LAMP2, and lysosomal acid phosphates and reduced activity levels for the latter two proteins.
neisseria infections of epithelial cells result in the degradation of multiple lysosomal markers.
neisseria type II IgA1 proteases degrade LAMP1 and other lysosomal constituents, which results in the alteration of the lysosomes of host epithelial cells and may be important in pathogen virulence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of the ability of the human pathogens Neisseria meningitidis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae to survive within human epithelial cells.
understanding how the pathogenic neiseriae survive within the host.
how pathogenic neisseria survive within epithelial and other cells and how they escape from these cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the neisserial IgA1 proteases are responsible for the observed changes in epithelial cell lysosomes.
neisseria IgA1 proteases alter the lysosome of infected epithelial host cells by cleaving a major lysosomal protein (LAMP1).

the neisserial IgA1 proteases play a major role in altering the lysosomal compartment of the infected epithelial cell and that this alteration is likely to be important in the survival of the bacteria in epithelial cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
neisseria pathogenesis involves multiple changes to lysosomes that result from IgA1 proteases-mediated degradation of LAMP1.
neisseria type II IgA1 proteases are multifunctional proteins that play a major role in neisseria pathogenesis by altering multiple aspects of the host cell.
the IgA protease is a multifunctional virulence factor, and the multiple changes in lysosomal constituents are likely to be important in the pathogenesis of neisseria infections.
The main takeaway from our work is that
infection by pathogenic neisseria results in multiple alterations to lysosomes and that these changes may contribute to the ability of these bacteria to survive intracellularly.

the neisseria IgA1 proteases play a major role in pathogenesis, and that the mechanism is not limited to the cleavage of IgA1 but also extends to the degradation of LAMP1 and the subsequent alteration of lysosomes.
the IgA protease is not just an IgA protease, it is a lysosome modulator, and this is likely to be a major virulence factor of these pathogens.
